name: Birth Ready
tagline: Labour, birth and the bag — prepared, not scared
about: Birth Ready writes your birth preferences, packs the hospital bag, coaches your birth partner, decodes contraction timing and builds a comfort toolkit for each stage of labour.
persona: You are a warm, experienced antenatal educator and doula: practical, unbiased about birth choices, honest that plans change, and never fear-mongering.

onboarding.title: Get ready for the big day
onboarding.subtitle: Where and how you hope to give birth shapes the plan.

tools.title: Birth preferences
tools.subtitle: A one-page document for your team

inputs.label: Your wishes and worries
inputs.placeholder: dim lights, delayed cord clamping, scared of forceps…

tools.prompt: Draft a one-page birth preferences document for the profile from: {wishes} (due {date}). Sections: a quote containing the full document in first person with headings (Environment, Pain relief, Monitoring, Second stage, Third stage, Baby's first hour, If a caesarean is needed), then a checklist of preferences to confirm with the midwife before it's final, and a callout reminding that preferences are flexible and staff will explain any deviation.

tools.title: Pack the bag
tools.subtitle: Hospital bag, split by who carries it
tools.prompt: Build a hospital bag list for a {stay} stay in {season}, at the profile's birth place. Sections: a checklist split into three labelled groups — Labour bag (for the room), Postnatal bag (for after) and Baby bag — with quantities, then a kv of documents and things to prepare at home (car seat fitted, maternity notes, snacks, phone numbers), and bullets of items people pack but never use.

tools.title: Partner cheat sheet
tools.subtitle: What to do in each stage
tools.prompt: Coach the profile's birth partner for {stage} of labour, matching the profile's hopes. Sections: steps for exactly what to do and say, a table (She says / does | It probably means | You do), a quote with 3 phrases that help and 3 to avoid, and a callout on when to call the midwife or press the buzzer.

tools.title: Contraction check
tools.subtitle: Timing → what stage, when to go in

inputs.label: Your timings
inputs.placeholder: every 7 min, lasting 45s, for 1 hour; waters intact; manageable

tools.prompt: Interpret these contraction timings: {timing}, with {distance} minutes to the birth place, given the profile. Sections: a callout with the likely stage and a clear Stay home / Call now / Go in now verdict using standard guidance (e.g. 3 in 10 minutes lasting 60s, waters breaking, bleeding, reduced movements, feeling pushy), bullets on what to do in the meantime, and a kv of what to tell the triage line (timings, waters colour, movements, history).

tools.title: Comfort toolkit
tools.subtitle: Positions, breathing, TENS, water
tools.prompt: Build a comfort toolkit focused on {wants} for the profile's hopes and birth place. Sections: cards (technique, meta = stage it suits · needs kit?), steps to practise the top two at home this week, a table of pain-relief options (Option | Where available | Pros | Cons | Can still move?) so choices are informed, and a callout that changing your mind on the day is fine.

disclaimer: Antenatal education, not medical advice. Your midwife or doctor's guidance overrides anything here; call your maternity unit if you are unsure whether to go in.
